items.title: Håkan Rydin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Glasgow, Scotland, July 27, 2016
items.q: The first time I played with him we were supposed to do a radio recording... We made a tour.

ctx.x: So he is very easy to play with. He also brought easy scores to read. I remember the first time, we hadn’t played that much but we played a couple of times. We made a tour. The first time I played with him we were supposed to do a radio recording, and at the same time a whole night at a jazz club, three sets or something like that. So we rehearsed. We rehearsed in the afternoon, and there was also two horns. So we got some arrangements. And it was a lot of things. I mean a whole night of music, it was a lot of…

And we rehearsed that song. And then when I came home at night after playing, of all this music, it was this song that went in my head. [humms] It’s a very, very simple song in a way, but still unique, it’s Tadd Dameron. I wrote it down, and he sang it very straight in a slow/medium tempo and with nothing special, but it was nice and it was a lot appreciated by the audience. And the day after, I told him this story. Do you know which song I was thinking about, it was “On a Misty Night.” And he said, “Yeah, that…
